narrative: Nvidia's Arm-based N1/N1X, unveiled June 1 at Computex, are positioned explicitly as on-device inference silicon - the standard N1 at 2,048-2,560 CUDA cores and 18-45W, the flagship N1X at 6,144 cores and 45-80W, co-designed with Microsoft to run an agentic assistant locally - while Nvidia simultaneously holds the data-center training/accelerator layer and licensed Groq inference IP, extending the divergent training-versus-inference compute profiles down to the client edge.
remaining_gap: The landing concerns hyperscaler in-house silicon (TPU, Trainium, MAIA, MTIA) bifurcating into separate part numbers; Nvidia is a merchant vendor pushing into client inference, not the hyperscaler-SKU split.
